Chapter 7: Prioritizing What Matters Most.
If you’re like most leaders, your days are packed with demands competing for your attention. The real challenge? Figuring out what truly deserves your focus. Not every task is created equal—some move you forward, while others just fill up your calendar.
Here’s a simple way to think about it: picture a jar, and imagine you need to fit in rocks, pebbles, and sand. If you start with the sand—those little, less important things—you won’t have room for the big rocks, which are your most important tasks. But if you put those big rocks in first, everything else can settle around them.
So, what are your big rocks? As a leader, it’s your job to spot them and make sure they get your time and energy.
Let’s talk about a few key strategies that can make prioritizing a lot easier:
First, get clear on your goals and values. When you know what matters most, it’s much simpler to make decisions about where to spend your energy.
Next, delegate or even eliminate those low-impact tasks. The less time you spend on things that don’t really matter, the more you have for work that truly moves the needle.
And don’t forget to set boundaries. Protect the time you need for strategic thinking and for building important relationships—these are often the areas that drive real progress.
Think about a nonprofit director, for example. Their inbox is overflowing, and meetings fill up the calendar. But deep down, they know that building partnerships and finding funding are what actually create impact. By blocking off time for these big priorities, and sharing or delegating those administrative tasks, they can make sure their focus stays where it matters most.
Here’s something to keep in mind—prioritization isn’t just a one-and-done decision. It’s an ongoing process. You’ll need to regularly check in on your commitments, adjust your plans, and clearly communicate what’s most important to your team.
When everyone knows what the priorities are, it’s so much easier to stay aligned and focused, even during the busiest or most stressful times.
